paragraphs.text: 第三方适配插件：把上游 REA（github.com/morluto/rea）的 MCP 服务接入 DeepSeek Harness，提供 mcp__rea__* 工具。2.x 会自动准备 Node、
REA CLI、JDK 与 Ghidra 并把那一行接好；逆向分析能力全部由上游 REA 提供。
# dsh-plugin-rea
**English** · 简体中文
> **Which version is this? 2.x — and `main` is it.** 2.x provisions the runtime itself (Node, the RE

A CLI, a
> JDK, Ghidra) and then wires the row: install the plugin, run `scripts/setup.mjs` once, re

start dsh.
> **1.x** is the older configuration-only adapter — it expects `rea` on PATH and Ghidra i

nstalled by you —
> kept on the `v1` branch and on npm as `dsh-plugin-rea@1.0.6`.
> Full comparison:
Two lines: 1.x and 2.x · upgrading: Upgrading from 1.x.
> REA **6.8.0** — this package's pin — still accepts Ghidra **12.1.x** only (12.2 is `unsupported`,

and the whole
> Ghidra decompile/analysis group disappears) and the jadx bridge **0.7.1** only (0.8.

0 fails on its first call with
> `Expected engine 0.7.1`, before any APK is loaded). Both gates were

re-checked against 6.8.0 on 2026-10-26 and
> neither one moved. JDK **21.0.13** is out upstream, bu

t Adoptium publishes no Windows build of it, so there is
> nothing to point at here — and it drops o

nly three of the four eMudhra anchors. The trade-off is therefore "all
> tools green, CVE still open

": Ghidra 12.1.4's CVE-2026-100504 / 100505 / 100503 / 113604 stay in the chain — **do
> not analyse
untrusted samples with this environment** — and the JDK still trusts the eMudhra anchors. Evidence,

> mitigations and revisit triggers: docs/update-review-2026-10-24.md and
> docs/update-review-2026-

10-26.md.
>
> **Ghidra 12.2 itself works** — measured 2026-10-26: same 9 segments, same 341 procedur

es, byte-identical `entry`
> pseudocode as 12.1.4, through REA's own bridge. What blocks it is REA's

version-equality check, not the bridge.
[该节后续省略]
## What this is
A **Cordis bundle with a provisioning layer**. `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, and that

patch
inserts one row of the official MCP client plugin (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`). The row lau

nches
`bin/rea-shim.mjs` with the running Node executable; the shim reads the machine-local state th

at
`scripts/setup.mjs` wrote and starts the REA CLI it provisioned. There is no analysis code here,

and the
published patch contains no machine path.
> **Third-party adapter.** This repository is not part of REA, ships none of REA's code, and is not
> maintained by REA's authors. It composes one configuration row and fetches upstream's own releases

.
> Upstream: github.com/morluto/rea (MIT) ·
> docs ·
> rea.tools · npm package `rea-agents`.
> REA'

s own problems go to its tracker; **this plugin's** problems go to
> this repository's issues.
**It adds exactly three things:** the tool registration under the `mcp__rea__*` names, the per-machi

ne
engine environment (`GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR`, `JAVA_HOME`, `REA_ADB_PATH`, `REA_APKTOOL_COMMAND`,
`RE
A_JADX_MCP_JAR`, `REA_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE`, …) scoped to that MCP child instead of the whole harness,

and
the provisioning that puts those components on disk.
## What it can and cannot do
The analysis is upstream's; this section only restates upstream's own contract so expectations are r
nalysis is upstream's; this section only restates upstream's own contract so expectations are right.

- **It cannot recover complete source code.** For native binaries upstream returns *pseudocode and
a
ssembly*, for Android APKs *decompiled methods*, for JEB units *pseudocode*, and for JavaScript/Elec

tron
*modules and their relations*. Upstream's tool contract states the pseudocode "is decompiler ou

tput, not
original source and not text-equivalent" to another provider's output.
- Not recoverable i

n practice: original identifier names, types, comments, macros and template expansion,
build scripts

and assets. Optimisation (inlining, reordering), symbol stripping, obfuscation, packing and
VM prot

ection only make the output worse.
[该节后续省略]
## Scope and caveats

- REA exposes 229 tools at 6.8.0, so every session's tool list grows.
- Provisioning is honest about

checksums: where a vendor publishes one it is pinned and verified; where none
exists (jadx-headless

-mcp, the apktool wrapper, Android platform-tools, the rolling "latest" URLs) the
hash is **measured

once and recorded**, and later drift is reported rather than silently accepted.
`bundle.json` lists

which components are in that state under `unverifiedChecksums`.
- Downloads are slow on some networ

ks (measured 0.35–0.54 MiB/s from the GitHub release CDN here, so Ghidra
alone takes ~25–45 min). Fe

tching is resumable on both routes: a partial `.part` is continued with a Range
request, and a `.par

t` that already holds the whole file is verified and kept instead of re-fetched.
- Some REA tools la

unch processes, write files and access the network — DSH's permission policy applies.
Analyse only a

rtifacts you are authorized to inspect.
- The MCP child and the engines it launches are ordinary pro

cesses running as **you**. DSH's tool
approvals govern what the model asks for, not what that child

ux, upstream's process-ownership checks need a **procps-compatible `ps`** on PATH; the
Ghidra/JADX a

nd firmware paths use it. A minimal image without it fails those tools, not the install.
- `scripts/

setup.mjs` resolves the REA CLI's closure with **`npm ci`** against the shipped
`scripts/vendor-lock

/` (`package.json` + `package-lock.json`). REA pins zod **exactly** (`"4.4.3"`), and 4.4.3 is
inside
GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5, so the closure is raised through `overrides` to **zod 4.6.7 / minimatch 11.0.5

/
glob 14.0.4**. `npm ci` verifies every tarball's sha512; if a repackaging mirror makes that fail

with `EINTEGRITY`,
it falls back to "same versions via overrides + `npm install`" (same versions, no

t byte-reproducible, and the log
says so). After landing, the version in `node_modules/zod/package.j

son` is read once more and anything below 4.6.6
is refused. `node scripts/check-dependency-advisorie

s.mjs` is the offline gate, wired into CI.
[该节后续省略]
